correctness.rationale: Complete finite enumeration: for connected three-uniform hypergraphs the program checks all 11 four-vertex and 958 five-vertex labeled hypergraphs and every absent triple, and after exact justified complement reduction all 128 and 73,760 binary representative comparisons. The three-vertex case is vacuous because the only connected triple has no missing triple. All calculations use exact fractions and positive-definite integer matrices. An explicit six-vertex connected three-edge witness has exact binary equilibrium and the algebraic formula 2t(553t+424)/(8427(19t+53)^2)>0 for every t>0; matrix coefficient checks independently certify that identity. The connectivity lower bound makes three original triples minimal.

originality.rationale: The 2023 Xu–Zhang paper supplies the very projection and polarization definition; its inspected Sections III–V give comparisons between directed and undirected projections, not the sharp order-six cutoff for adding one homogeneous three-person group to a connected triple-only network with binary innate opinions. The 2022 Rácz–Rigobon pairwise-edge sensitivity theorem covers the general nonmonotonic mechanism but gives no equivalently quantified triple-only minimum. Relevant mathematical-record searches and accessible related claims showed no covering finite classification. Bibliographic equivalence elsewhere remains possible.

value.rationale: The question is motivated by whether beneficial-looking additional homogeneous group communication necessarily reduces opinion polarization. The answer gives a sharp minimum population for pure three-person-group networks under natural binary opinions and uniform weights, supplies an exact minimally connected witness, and shows the reversal is robust over all positive new-group weights. The result distinguishes single-group addition from arbitrary pairwise edge changes. Its exact finite boundary is useful independently of general graph classifications, without claiming broad downstream applications.
